I have farmed this land a long time, and with only 7.5 mu and two people in the house, I will keep the plan simple and dependable. I will put 3 mu into cotton because cotton is still my main crop, and I know how to manage it well. On the other 4.5 mu, I will do the usual winter wheat followed by summer maize, because that rotation fits Quzhou County, makes good use of my well irrigation, and gives me grain and cash flow. I will use better seed on all three crops because the land is small, so I need stable emergence, better yield, and less risk. I will not push inputs too hard, but I will not farm too lightly either. I will give wheat enough fertilizer and water because it responds well and is reliable with irrigation. I will give maize moderate to strong fertilizer because it follows wheat and needs support for yield. For cotton, I will control fertilizer and water more carefully so it does not grow too rank, and I will spray more often there because insects are usually the bigger problem. For tillage, I will plough the cotton ground once to make a clean seedbed, use rotary tillage for wheat, and use no-tillage for maize after wheat to save labor and catch the season on time.
